hosts.iamcredentials.googleapis.com: Every operation that matters here mints a credential for a service account: an access token, an ID token, a signed JWT or a signed blob. The three GETs (allowed locations) are not worth a hole.
hosts.sts.googleapis.com: Security Token Service: exchanges one credential for a Google access token. Its whole purpose is to return a token.
hosts.oauth2.googleapis.com: The OAuth token endpoint. frisket answers /token itself for the placeholder; nothing else here should reach Google with the real token behind it.
hosts.securetoken.googleapis.com: Firebase's token service: exchanges a refresh token for an ID token.

setIamPolicy.reason: Replaces who may do what on the resource: it can widen access, including to allUsers.

getIamPolicy.reason: Reads the policy; a POST on many APIs, and changes nothing.

testIamPermissions.reason: Asks which of the named permissions the caller holds; a POST, and changes nothing.

forbidden.iam.projects.serviceAccounts.keys.create: Returns the new key's privateKeyData: a service account private key, usable anywhere, for up to its expiry (by default never).
forbidden.iam.projects.serviceAccounts.signBlob: Deprecated IAM v1 signing: returns a blob signed with the service account's system-managed key (a signed URL is one of these).
forbidden.iam.projects.serviceAccounts.signJwt: Deprecated IAM v1 signing: returns a JWT signed as the service account, exchangeable for an access token.
forbidden.iam.projects.locations.oauthClients.cred: Returns the new OAuth client's clientSecret (Output only, system-generated).
Returns the OAuth client credential with its clientSecret: the description says the secret is output, not that it is withheld on reads.
Lists OAuth client credentials with their clientSecrets.
Returns the updated OAuth client credential, clientSecret included.
A GET that returns the secret's payload: the value itself, not metadata about it.
forbidden.secretmanager.projects.locations.secrets: A GET that returns the secret's payload: the value itself, not metadata about it.
forbidden.storage.projects.hmacKeys.create: Returns the new HMAC key's secret: an S3-style credential for the service account, which signs its own requests and so can never be carried by frisket.

guarded.iam.projects.serviceAccounts.keys.upload: Adds a public key the caller holds the private half of: a new standing credential for the service account.
guarded.iam.projects.serviceAccounts.enable: Brings a disabled service account back into use, with every key it has.
guarded.iam.projects.serviceAccounts.keys.enable: Brings a disabled key back into use.
guarded.iam.projects.serviceAccounts.undelete: Restores a deleted service account and its bindings.
guarded.storage.bucketAccessControls.insert: Grants an entity (a user, a group, allUsers) access to the bucket.
guarded.storage.bucketAccessControls.patch: Changes an entity's access to the bucket.
guarded.storage.bucketAccessControls.update: Changes an entity's access to the bucket.
guarded.storage.defaultObjectAccessControls.inse: Grants an entity access to every new object in the bucket.
guarded.storage.defaultObjectAccessControls.patc: Changes an entity's access to every new object in the bucket.
guarded.storage.defaultObjectAccessControls.upda: Changes an entity's access to every new object in the bucket.
guarded.storage.objectAccessControls.insert: Grants an entity (allUsers included) access to the object.
guarded.storage.objectAccessControls.patch: Changes an entity's access to the object.
guarded.storage.objectAccessControls.update: Changes an entity's access to the object.
guarded.storage.buckets.lockRetentionPolicy: Locks the retention policy permanently: it cannot be removed or shortened again.
guarded.storage.folders.deleteRecursive: Deletes a folder and everything under it.
guarded.compute.instances.setMetadata: Instance metadata carries ssh-keys and startup scripts: this can add a login or run code as root on the instance.
guarded.compute.projects.setCommonInstanceMetada: Project metadata carries ssh-keys for every instance in the project.
guarded.compute.instances.setServiceAccount: Attaches a service account, and its access, to the instance.

read.pubsub.projects.schemas.validate: Validates a schema definition; a POST, and creates nothing.
read.pubsub.projects.schemas.validateMessage: Validates a message against a schema; a POST, and publishes nothing.

google.pubsub.v1.Subscriber.StreamingPul.reason: Pull by stream: leases and acknowledges messages, as Pull does. Bidirectional, so its body never ends and it cannot be asked: allow or refuse only.

google.storage.v2.Storage.ReadObject.reason: No google.api.http rule: gRPC only. Server-streaming; the request is one message.

google.storage.v2.Storage.BidiReadObject.reason: No google.api.http rule: gRPC only. Bidirectional reads of one object.

google.storage.v2.Storage.QueryWriteStat.reason: No google.api.http rule: gRPC only. Says how much of a resumable write has arrived.

google.storage.v2.Storage.SetIamPolicy.reason: Replaces who may do what on the bucket or object.

google.storage.v2.Storage.UpdateBucket.reason: No google.api.http rule: gRPC only. Can change the bucket's ACLs.

google.storage.v2.Storage.UpdateObject.reason: No google.api.http rule: gRPC only. Can change the object's ACL.

google.storage.v2.Storage.WriteObject.reason: Client-streaming upload: the body ends, but may exceed what frisket reads to ask.

google.storage.v2.Storage.BidiWriteObjec.reason: Bidirectional upload: its body never ends while it waits, so it cannot be asked.
